findings.claim: With Task 6 now required, the headline promises about 31 minutes in a 35-minute block, stated without the 'authoring estimate' label that lab.json carries; the figure is about half the lab's earlier authored median (60) and covers task work only, so README reading and the one-time Playwright/Chromium setup eat most of the 4-minute buffer for an average learner. Evidence: README line 3: 'together they are sized to finish in about 31 minutes with a small buffer left over inside the block'. lab.json minutes {estimatedMedian 31, cap 35}; notes: 'about 27 minutes for tasks 1 to 5 ... plus about 4 minutes for Task 6 ... Neither number is a measured learner pilot.'. authoring/evidence/html-css-js/dom-tooling-and-async/timing-critic-education-recheck.json edu-t2 records the earlier halving (60 to about 25) of this lab's median. Intake section Minute budgets: S25 is a Concept day whose platform coding practice is Faded then fresh 40 plus 7 of Short exercises, so a modestly larger cap still fits.
findings.recommendation: Label the README figure an authoring estimate (not a measured pilot) and state whether setup happens before the block; consider cap 40 (inside S25's 40-minute Faded-then-fresh block) to give average learners a real buffer now that every task is required.

findings.claim: The headline calls S25 a 'Lab day', but the frozen calendar and intake list S25 as a Concept day; the lab occupies its platform coding-practice time, not a Lab-template Guided lab block. Learners and instructors may look for a Lab-day schedule that does not exist. Evidence: authoring/evidence/html-css-js/intake.md day table: 'S25 | Async and DevTools | Concept'. Intake section Minute budgets: S20, S22, S24, S25 use the Concept template. Catalog module.json note: lab 'added on the S25 block'.
findings.recommendation: Say 'Standard track, S25 (Concept day) lab block' or name the block it uses.
